name: Alsos
description: Alsos is a sophisticated Hungarian trick-taking game blending Jass structure with Tarokk-style announced figures. In the core three-player form one declarer plays against the other two.

overview.description: Alsos is a sophisticated Hungarian trick-taking game blending Jass structure with Tarokk-style announced figures. In the core three-player form one declarer plays against the other two.

history.origins: Alsos emerged in Budapest in the late 19th century and remained popular through the first half of the 20th century.
timeline: 1880s: Developed as a competitive alternative to simpler Jass games.
1930s: Standardized in G.J. Potter's card game manuals.
Mid-20th Century: Reached peak popularity in cafes and clubs across Hungary.
history.cultural: Regarded as one of the most intellectually stimulating games of central Europe, often compared to Bridge in its depth.
history.evolution: It evolved from Kalaber-style Ace-Ten play by adopting announced figures from Tarokk, adding heavy bidding and kontra depth.

setup.players: 3 active players. With 4 players, dealer sits out each hand.
setup.deck: 32 cards (A, K, Over, Under, 10, 9, 8, 7). Usually Hungarian suits (Acorns, Hearts, Leaves, Bells).
setup.dealing: Each player receives 9 cards (dealt in batches of 3-3-3). 5 cards remain in the 'Talon' (one face up to propose trump).

rules.objective: As declarer, score more points through tricks, melds, and 'figures' than the highest-scoring opponent.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Bidding**: Players bid to accept the turned-up trump or name a new suit/game (Betli, Klopitzky). 2. **Melding**: Before the first trick, players announce 'sequences' and 'Vannak' (four of a kind). 3. **The Play**: Declarer competes against the two opponents (who cooperate). 4. **Figures**: During play, players may announce 'Ultimo' (winning last trick with trump 7) or 'Volat' (winning all tricks).
keyRules: Trump Rank: Under (Alsos) highest, then 9, A, 10, K, Over, 8, 7.
No-Trump Rank: A, 10, K, Over, Under, 9, 8, 7.
Kontra: Opponents can double the score if they feel the declarer will lose. Declarer can 'Rekontra' to quadruple.

strategy.basic: Track the trump Under and 9 closely; those two cards control many contracts.
strategy.intermediate: When legal, use talon exchange carefully to convert weak cards into suit control before trick play.
strategy.advanced: Ultimo timing is critical: if opponents can force out your trumps early, last-trick plans collapse.
tips: Cooperation is key for opponents: if one partner has a weak hand, they should sacrifice high cards to their partner's tricks to ensure the declarer is outscored.
Betli (losing all tricks) is a high-reward defensive bid if you are dealt a hand with many 7s and 8s.

variations.name: Betli
variations.description: The declarer must lose every single trick. Worth 5 game points.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Betli uses the same core engine structure; its special win condition and scoring are captured in rules and scoring text rather than separate engine overrides.

variations.name: Klopitzky
variations.description: A 'no-trump' variation where every player plays for themselves for one hand.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Klopitzky changes scoring and objective but reuses the main engine loop; variation details are described in the rules instead of engine overrides.

scoring.description: Total points come from card values, melds, and figures.
scoring.winCondition: The declarer wins only if their total points exceed the points of BOTH opponents. If either opponent beats or ties the declarer, the declarer 'goes down'.

synthesis.shortDescription: One of the most complex and rewarding Central European card games. Battle as the declarer against two cooperating rivals. Use trumps, melds, and 'figures' like Ultimo to claim victory.

hero.title: ALSOS
hero.subtitle: The Hungarian Masterpiece
hero.tagline: A high-stakes fusion of Jass and Tarokk from Budapest card culture.
